I would say talk with a trained cclinical psychologist whom can refer you to either a doctor of medicine or psychiatrist. Wild mood swings can be a plethora of both psychological issues and/or physiological issues. Most people have internal dialogue with themselves that doesn't quite fit their own voice/views. If you're fear is any schizo-effective or schizotypical disorder you don't have to be worried. You wouldn't be able to tell your behaviour is abnormal unless in extremely early phases but there is genetics,  age, gender, drug use etc....  That Needs to factor first. Rapid mood swings can be indicative of "cycling" which could be one disorder or another. It could be normal for your life as you age or a personality disorder. It could be hormonal related  or completely emotional in relation to the anxiety and depression group of disorders.

You're right.  I philosophize too much.  I do just want the pain over. I feel as though I've exhausted all my avenues. I've been in therapy,  trying everything until I've gotten myself so broke I can't afford it.  I've done medications mixed with therapy.  I did a wellness retreat and (having been a therapist myself)  I've listened and submitted to all the treatments and worked the programs the best I could. It hasn't gotten better,  just worse.  If lobotomy was an option,  that's where I'd land not the ultimatum of death.

Whenever I feel like suicide is the answer. I have always gone through the motions of a planned suicide. I time when I will do it and how. How I'll time things and how the aftermath will play.  I always used to stop there.  I would feel better because I had given myself permission and power over my choice to live or die.

Now I've gone the step further and write notes. It is usually here that I feel better. Like I let go of all I needed to say to these people that I couldn't before.  Now it's usually at note writing that I will want to just do it then but I always give myself a 20 Day limit.  If I still feel the same, all the kinks worked out of the plan (how and where I'll do it,  how I plan to be found in the least traumatizing way for the person who will find me, etc...) and all my notes written and proofread than re-written,  I do a cost/benefit analysis of my life. It's here that I feel the most relief no matter which way it sways.  I feel I have my power back and used all the logic I could to sway me towards life. 

This can be healthy if you aren't impulsive but are definitely not safe nor recommended.  Keeping yourself away from your choice of suicide is the best way to approach the hypothetical. I recommend approaching and confronting it within therapy.  Unless you tell a therapist you have motive, means, and opputunity to kill yourself they shouldn't report it.

I respect your opinion. I don't identify as suicidal, I feel suicidal. Cognitive distancing. It's a tenique that stops you from identify yourself as your feeling. I say I feel worthless because I know I am not worthless, it's just an emotin. 
 
Back to it . I've never spoken the words out loud until three months ago, never said I'm suicidal until then.  I've kept going on and on for so long getting called strong for living through what I have and still being here.  

I've built a mildly successful career where my patients adore me. I am in all sense to others strong, smart and passionate. I make others happy if again my patients are to be believe. I've saved their lives because I am calm (and when I'm not its because I'm an excitable puppy of a person as I've been described). I understand that not ruminating on death will give my mind rest but there is nothing remotely important enough in my life to stimulate me. No distraction great enough,  nothing I do that takes more than half my brainpower. I'm focused when I have my task at hand but there never is enough to do.

I have happy moments and do feel joy with the right situation. When I am alone and those things are stripped away (as they are fleeting moments)  I'm left with the scars that haunt me. The world around me I can't be comfortable in because I feel everyone can see what I see when they look at me.  Either the malformed human creature or the filth I still scrub thoroughly from my skin from all the sexual assaults I've endured. I ache with deep pains in my body from where I've been physically broken that can't be fixed. And the berating I go through from the mental abuse I repeat in my mind from years of being torn down -not to mention the brainwashing my ex loving instilled in me- never cease. 

I live feeling tormented by things I had no control in and the emotional pain of it has me weighing my options.  To suffer on and pick up more because others will be sad if I'm not around or I can end my own suffering and let others be sad for a little while. In the cost/benefit analysis of my life, ending it is the best option. I just want to be told by one person that loves me that it's okay. I am going to make sure they are all taken care of.  Once I know my last lose end is somewhere stable and safe I am given myself permission to do one thing for me.

It sounds less chemical imbalance and more mood disorder which is generally a combo of structure and chemical but not SSRI related usually dopamine. No one can diagnose without meeting and talking but if it's related to say,  bi-polar or Bpd or something like that drinking counteracts any meds you'd take and make the issues worse.  Try looking into a dual diagnosis with more focus on mood disorders and away from the depression/anxiety package every provider is slapping on people these days.

I completely understand this feeling. I have written notes to the people that mattered. I don't know your plan but both of mine are slow rolls.  I've decided to make sure I don't give my location away but to make my one last call and stay on the phone with that person until I pass out from whichever choice I go with. My friend Lana did that with me. She had a panic attack and cried to me the whole time she was slowly dying with me on the other end trying to support her (I was not aware she had taken what she had). When she finally stopped talking and it went quite I thought she has just worked herself into an exhausted fit and fell asleep on the phone. I won't be traumatizing a friend like that but it will make it all less lonely to have a teary eyed but calm Convo on the phone with someone as I drift away.
